answer: A Harberger-tax registry makes identity slots self-priced: each agent declares its slot's value and pays a recurring tax on it, and anyone may buy the slot at the declared price. A sybil farmer hoarding a grove of fake agents must pay tax on every identity or price them so low that rivals buy them out; there is no canyon to hide in, because the cost scales linearly with the herd while honest agents hold one slot each. The attacker's profit hits its nadir the moment the tax exceeds the value of one more fake identity.
